reason: Pairing hydrogen nuclei with electrons should begin forming the neutral gas needed for the goals.
expectation: I expect neutral hydrogen to form, possibly helping light travel; I’m unsure whether this alone completes either goal.

alternatives.reason: Helium can also capture electrons, but I chose to start with hydrogen.

effect: Neutral hydrogen has formed; helium capture is the only offered combination left.
reaction: The distinction between making an atom and making a new element is useful.
reason: I’ll follow the only available combination to form neutral helium.
expectation: I expect helium nuclei to capture electrons and form neutral helium, though I’m unsure whether that advances a goal immediately.

effect: Neutral helium has formed, and combining the two neutral gases is now the only offered action.
reaction: The clarification that the icon represents full recombination is helpful.
reason: I’ll combine the neutral gases to work toward gathering star-making gas.
expectation: I expect a mixture of neutral hydrogen and helium, though I’m unsure whether it will complete a goal.

effect: The neutral atoms now form primordial gas, which can be used toward either goal.
reaction: The reminder that this gas contains no rock or water puts later world-building in perspective.
reason: I’ll combine the gas with trapped radiation to work toward letting light travel.
expectation: I expect the radiation to become free to travel through the neutral gas, though I’m unsure how the game will represent it.

alternatives.reason: The denser patch seems useful for gathering star-making gas, but I’ll pursue the light goal first.

effect: Neutral gas allows ancient light to travel, completing the light goal; the gas-gathering goal remains.
reaction: The explanation that light travels more freely because fewer electrons scatter it is helpful.
reason: I’ll use the denser patch to work toward gathering the first star-making gas.
expectation: I expect gas to collect in the denser region, possibly completing the remaining goal.

alternatives.reason: Expansion may change the travelling light, but I’ll pursue the remaining goal first.

effect: Gravity gathered the primordial gas and completed the remaining goal; further contraction would require the knot to lose heat.
reaction: The distinction between bound regions and the continuing expansion elsewhere was interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Freeing the ancient light was most worthwhile: the explanation connected neutral atoms to reduced scattering and a transparent universe.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining the two neutral gases felt relatively routine, though it established the primordial mixture.

surprise.text: I was surprised that a dense gas knot must lose heat to contract much further, and that bound regions need not expand with the universe.

arbitrary.text: Combining primordial gas with trapped radiation was a somewhat abstract representation, though the result explained its purpose clearly.

continue.text: Yes. I’d like to see how the gas knot becomes the stars and materials needed for a world; the explanations made the processes engaging.
